gate_results.gate_id: D2-006-G5: Cost drag <= 50% of gross PnL

observations: RETROSPECTIVE: this report was authored after execution as part of WP-6c. Metrics are transcribed from DEC-0001, the H-001 trial_log entry, and the H-001 experiment notebook. H-001 produced negative full-period Sharpe of -0.3897788502290693, max drawdown of 178.1316%, and cost drag of 251.8278% of gross PnL. The strategy failed 7 of 8 D2-006 gates; the short leg lost materially while the long leg was profitable, and DEC-0001 archived the candidate as a baseline NO-GO. Max-drawdown and cost-drag values are under pre-WP-5b pipeline semantics; per WP-5a/WP-5b audit conclusions the overall NO-GO verdict is unaffected by later pipeline fixes.
diagnostic_findings: Naive symmetric funding-directional logic on 4h bars is not promotable under current cost, drawdown, Sharpe, and concentration gates.
Funding receipts dominated the final equity result, but the equity path was unstable and risk-adjusted performance was negative.
The short leg lost money materially while the long leg was profitable, so symmetric funding-directional exposure did not behave as a balanced edge.
The H-001 result contributed to the WP-4a failure-analysis conclusion that future funding work needs independent confirmation or materially different risk design.
Any future funding-directional variant should be pre-registered separately with a fresh rationale, parameter budget, and risk-control design.
